test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 03 Aug, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Mohan purchased trousers for Rs. 765, after a discount of 15% was offered on its marked price. What is the marked price (in Rs.) of the trousers?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Fraction value of 15% discount = −3/20, meaning Marked Price (MP) = 20 units and Selling Price (SP) = 17 units.

Given SP = 17 units = Rs. 765

1 unit = 765 ÷ 17 = Rs. 45

MP = 20 units = 45 × 20 = 900

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of trousers = Rs. 765

Discount offered = 15%

**Formula Used:**

MP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)]

 
 Marked Price
 100%

 
 Selling Price
 85% = Rs. 765

 
• 
 

 − 15% Discount

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100%.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100% − 15% = 85%

⇒ According to the question, 85% of MP = Rs. 765

⇒ MP = 765 × (100 ÷ 85)

⇒ MP = 765 × (20 ÷ 17)

⇒ MP = 45 × 20 = 900

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) while Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise.

Relationship between MP and CP

If a profit of P% is made after allowing a discount of D%, then the ratio of MP to CP is determined by MP ÷ CP = (100 + P) ÷ (100 − D).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the equivalent single discount given is (a + b − a×b ÷ 100)%.
